name: afero-768f1fb0-blind25-ots
instr:
# Afero: wrong answers from wildcard lookups, archives, overlays and temp paths — diagnosing without a test suite

An application built on this library asks a storage layer what it holds and moves bytes in and out of it, and it now gets both of those wrong in many places. Nothing about the callers changed and nothing about how things are laid out on disk changed. The same requests that used to be answered correctly are answered wrongly, and in several places a request that used to be served is refused outright.

Looking things up by name gives unreliable answers. A wildcard pattern that contains no wildcard characters at all — a plain name that really is present — comes back with nothing, while the same request made with a name that is absent hands that name straight back as though it had been found; a link pointing at something real and a link whose destination was deleted both come back with nothing. Any pattern that does contain a wildcard now yields nothing at all, on every kind of storage we tried, real disk, in-memory and both archive kinds alike, where it used to list the children under the directory part of the pattern. Inside one kind of archive, a member asked for by a name that is not in canonical form — the root of the archive itself, or a name carrying a doubled separator or a dot segment — no longer resolves, so descending through an archive that stores no explicit directory entries misses things and listing its root comes back short. A view built to sift names
